entries.text: He won't be asking for it tonight. You can tell him Miss Clara said so.
It's Marco, isn't it? I used to be given bread here when I was small.
What does the letter say, Julian?
Doctor Moreau. Before you open that bag, there is something you need to hear.
Roll up your sleeve, Mr Edmund Hale.
Without that bottle you won't last ten minutes once an attack starts. So never take it out of the drawer.
I sent someone to your old hospital. I've read the winter of 1907. And the line you altered.
The face in that newspaper was Doctor Moreau. Two patients dead, and the record altered, it said. The name of that hospital was stamped on a brown bottle too.
The wall clock says fourteen minutes past eight. Sixteen minutes until the dinner bell.
Right-hand drawer. Brown bottle. Twenty-four tablets. I brought ones exactly the same colour, so no one will know the difference.
Twelve sugar pills. They do dissolve under the tongue. They simply do nothing to the heart.
The right-hand drawer of the study desk. The real bottle that was in it I carried out, and the bottle in that drawer now is mine.
Wait. There's a brown glass bottle shoved under the coal bin. Ash heaped over it, but the label didn't burn. St Allen Sanatorium, it says.
Sir — a moment ago I saw Doctor Moreau come out of the cellar door, in the corridor. There was coal dust on her skirt.
